item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While I get that references to Valhalla and Ragnarok and other Norse mythological themes might be pushing the envelope a bit for what is practical, and this article is certainly rife with them, I didn't get that this was "broken and sending people out (…) early."

I read this as some kind of cosmic version of an FPS King of the Hill scenario. Since many of the arrivals don't actually leave, and frequently only fire upon Foundation personnel when they approach too close or as the result of counterfire, they appear at dawn and vanish at dusk, and it's…well, it's on a hill, I view it as more of some anomalous "game," keeping "entities" entertained.

For a hill, men would kill, why? They do not know.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The name of the AC-130 gives it away for those who don't see it before.

I'm unimpressed. I don't think Valhalla should be skipified, and, if it is, it needs to be done better than this. I mean, we have Giraffe Hell and Ice Cream Hell, and both of those are more fun to read (or, were more fun to read for me, rather) than this was. The implication that Valhalla is broken and sending people out to Ragnarok early is interesting, and I understand that the Foundation can't know everything, but this left me unsatisfied.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My Norse mythology obsession has brought me an interesting question. These -seem- to be pretty obviously Einherjar. If they're returning to Midgard, and they are killed again..

Does Odin get two for the price of one? Is he trying to cheat Ragnarok by increasing the number of his host? I know this is probably not what was intended, but I can't shake the idea. Granted, due to the nature of Norse myth, it won't work.

Alright, enough rambling.

item.content:encoded:
I always thought it was similar to the redacted weapon used in http://www.scp-wiki.net/scp-514. Implying the foundation probably has access to some crazy tech-weapons, and whatever team that appeared was one that died while containing a Keter or particular bad Euclid object. I mean, an entrenched battle-ready company took 14 casualties just containing this platoon sized force until air support arrived, there must have been something going on beyond just "this dead MTF with their assault rifles were a bunch of badasses". It's not a bad expungement.

Edit: Although I guess the casualty figures are left over from when the final one was a Mysterious Horde of 300 rather than an MTF team. I forgot that was what it originally was! I like the dead MTF team better.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Artillery would be cheaper than flying planes every day, and you only need one barrage to wipe out a hillside. AC-130s are also expensive and limited in number, and also visible from a long way off. Artillery testing range makes as much sense as the existing cover story. Just having one AC-130 would be an improvement, although still pushing it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nah, given the circumstances I don't think that is so bad. Besides, what will draw more outside attention, a quick airstrike or a sustained artillery barrage? Also given that they never know what will pop out of that location I think the flexibility of air support would be better than artillery.

Also they don't need to fight the spawned soldiers most of the time, it's not like there's a war every night.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: A squadron of AC-130s? Really? Sounds like tacticoolness for tacticoolness' sake to me, especially when it'd be cheaper just to put the artillery on the ground. Not like the hill is moving. I also have to wonder how much of the hill is left after being subjected to daily bombardment for years.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Awesome SCP. I would suggest that documentation of attempts at communicating with some of the "armies" that appear be provided. Do they understand what's going on? Are they being transported from a similar place? Have any come through unprepared to fight (i.e. camped on a battleground or simply not on the front lines)?
There is a lot of room for development on this one, including some cross-SCP experimentation.
